evidence: Zinc oxide layer was grown by ALD technique in a Beneq TFS-500 reactor using diethylzinc (DEZn) and water as reactant gases. The deposition was conducted at 85 /compBC and 250 /compBC temperatures (for membranes with and without the supporting ring, respectively), and the pressure in the reactor was kept at about 4 Torr. Nitrogen was used as a carrier gas to transport precursor vapors to the sample surface and purge reaction gases from the reactor during each reaction half-cycle. Different cycle length was used, depending on the sample type. Firstly, ZnO layer was grown at 220 /compBC on a flat and clean silicon wafer, in order to evaluate the layer parameters and the ALD process itself. In this case, 0.25 s precursor pulse and 0.5 s purge pulse (the same for both precursors) were used. This cycle, 1.5 seconds long, was enough to reach conditions for self terminating reactions of ALD process. In the case of samples with nanopores, the cycle was extended several times, trying different precursor and purge pulse lengths, in order to reach the same growth rate and uniformity inside the deep nanopore. A typical cross-flow configuration was used for silicon samples, with precursors flow over the surface of the substrate.
